packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-07 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure: no proposed identification or prior reading of this fragment was in my context. I did nothing beyond the brief: I read PROMPT.md and viewed image-001 to image-012. All twelve images loaded. (I ran one directory listing of the packet folder to see the filenames. I did not open packet.json.)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)

Face A (overview image-001; tiles image-002 to image-007)
- A narrow vertical parchment strip, roughly 9 x 25 cm against the ruler, upright. It is severely abraded, the ink is faded to grey, and there are worm/stain holes. The lower half is almost blank or rubbed.
- There is a broad vertical dark band down the middle and a horizontal dark band about a third of the way down (image-001, y~570) and another lower (y~1110). These look like offset/glue or binding-strip marks, not ruling. This is an observation; the cause is my interpretation.
- Text is in two areas:
  (a) Left of the vertical band: about 12 lines of small cursive gothic, cropped at the left edge (image-002). It ends just above the horizontal band. Below the band, around image-004 y~500-660, a few more faint lines.
  (b) Right of the vertical band: an upper block whose first two lines (image-003 top) look like a heading or running line ("De b..."/"cap..."), in a slightly larger or different hand, followed by about 12 lines. Lower right (image-005): a separate block of short lines, each preceded by a paragraph-like sign or "C"-shaped mark in the left margin (image-005 at y~290, 550, 740, 860, 1050). The lines are cut off at the right edge of the leaf.
- Whether (a) and (b) are two columns of one page, or text and gloss, is uncertain. The left text runs under the vertical band and seems to continue into the right area on some lines, so this may be one column of text crossing the band. I cannot settle it.
- No colour can be distinguished. No enlarged initials beyond the marginal signs in image-005.

Face B (overview image-008; tiles image-009 to image-012)
- The same strip from the other side, upright. One block of text at the upper left, cut at the left edge (first letters lost on many lines). The right half of the strip is largely blank, apart from a boxed or ruled numeral-like group at mid-height (image-009, approx. "IIII c" with a cross, inside a ruled box) and a few scattered strokes.
- The lines vary in size and spacing. There are short interlinear additions in smaller script (image-010 y~605; image-011 y~260, 470, 520). The look is note-like or verse-like rather than a regular written block. This is an impression only.
- Script: gothic cursive/textualis with long descenders (f, s, p). In one place (image-010 y~240) a whole line is smudged or struck through, apparently a deliberate cancellation.
- Most legible zone: image-010 bottom to image-011 middle.

SELECTED SPANS
I selected the readable left-edge block of Face B (image-009, image-010, image-011), the Face A heading (image-003 top), and line openings in Face A (image-002, image-005). Unread or illegible: the lower half of both faces; most of the Face A right block; and the right ends of all lines (lost to the trim on Face A, faded on Face B).
Overlaps: image-010 repeats the last two lines of image-009 ("in fac.. forme..." and "duplice..."), and image-011 repeats the last lines of image-010 ("..nj vis..."). I count each line once and label it from the tile where I read it best.

LIMITATIONS
- Ink is heavily faded and the surface is abraded on both faces. On Face A almost all words are tentative; my effort there gave a heading fragment and a few isolated words, not connected prose.
- Face A is cut at the right edge (line ends lost) and at the left of the left text. Face B is cut at the left edge (line beginnings lost).
- The relation of the two text areas on Face A is uncertain (two columns, or one column crossing the dark band, or text plus annotation).
- Face B's lines are irregular, with interlinear additions and a cancelled line, so the order of the main and added text is uncertain.
- The line numbers are positional (counted from the top of each tile by y-coordinate). Blank or illegible lines between them are not always numbered separately.
- Suggestion: multispectral/UV imaging, or a raking-light capture of Face A, would be needed for any connected reading. A higher-contrast version of image-010 and image-011 might secure Face B's lines L3-L8.
